comment: Shared allowlist/suppression config for the public-release audits. Deep-merges over the defaults embedded in scripts/audit_common.py. Review this file whenever the audit surfaces new findings; never silence findings by deleting the config. Allowlisted values are fabricated test fixtures (fake addresses/phone/coordinates in tests and Massachusetts ingest fixtures), the GitHub noreply committer address used for synthetic PR merge-ref commits, and '2018 Constitutional Court' (a court name, not a street address; false positive of the street-address pattern).

allowlist.tax_ids_comment: Manufacturer product identifiers on device records (UPC/EAN barcodes and article numbers), reviewed 2026-08-08 and confirmed to be published product codes, not tax or parcel numbers. PII-005 flags any long numeric run for human review; these are the reviewed dispositions. Add an entry only after confirming the number is a manufacturer-published product identifier.
allowlist.addresses_comment: Reviewed false positives. 'Constitutional Court' matches the street-suffix pattern in legal citations such as 'the 2018 Constitutional Court ruling'; it is a court, not a street. The remaining entries are synthetic Massachusetts test-fixture addresses. Reviewed 2026-08-09. Add an entry only after confirming the match is not a real premises address.
allowlist.emails_comment: noreply@github.com and @users.noreply.github.com are GitHub-generated, non-personal addresses. beau@boorman.tech is the maintainer's own git committer identity, present in the author/committer field of every commit in this repository and already public in the GitHub commit log; it is not leaked third-party PII. Reviewed 2026-08-09.
allowlist.phones_comment: 555-01xx is the NANP block reserved for fictional use; such numbers cannot be assigned to a real subscriber and appear here only in test fixtures. 617-555-0199 is the specific fixture instance. Reviewed 2026-08-09.

suppressions_comment: Self-detection only. audit_sensitive_content.py contains the PII regex definitions themselves, and test_sensitive_content_classification.py contains the synthetic PII-shaped fixtures that prove those regexes fire — including the negative controls that keep the business-contact rule from under-flagging. Scanning either file reports the detector, not a leak. Reviewed 2026-08-09.
suppressions_history_comment: ACKNOWLEDGED, NOT RESOLVED — expires when this repository goes public. The three LARGE-004 entries above are ~79 MiB of California DCC licensee data that remains reachable in git history after 6d740f4 untracked it from the working tree; verification on 2026-08-09 recovered 20,697 email addresses from a single blob via `git show`. They are suppressed ONLY because this repository is private, so the exposure is bounded to people who already have access. This is a conscious deferral recorded so CI does not block contributors while the maintainer decides. It is NOT a disposition. Execute docs/history-cleanup-plan.md and DELETE these three entries before making the repository public — doing otherwise publishes the data. Tracked as a [BLOCKER] in docs/pre-publication-checklist.md. Reviewed 2026-08-09.
